claim: Notch activity initiates in a stripe of cells flanking the mesoderm, the mesectoderm (MSE), in the last cycle prior to gastrulation (nuclear cycle 14, nc14).
source: Notch activity initiates in a stripe of cells flanking the mesoderm, the mesectoderm (MSE), in the last cycle prior to gastrulation (nuclear cycle 14, nc14), and remains active throughout gastrulation.
evidence: This is stated directly in the manuscript text describing when and where Notch activity begins in the Drosophila embryo.

claim: Notch activity remains active throughout gastrulation in the mesectoderm.
source: Notch activity initiates in a stripe of cells flanking the mesoderm, the mesectoderm (MSE), in the last cycle prior to gastrulation (nuclear cycle 14, nc14), and remains active throughout gastrulation.
evidence: This is stated directly in the manuscript text describing the temporal pattern of Notch activity.

claim: Mesectoderm cells divide after gastrulation, change their polarity and form a boundary that separates the flanking neuroectoderm.
source: These cells divide after gastrulation, change their polarity and form a boundary that separates the flanking neuroectoderm (Yu et al., 2021).
evidence: This is stated directly in the manuscript text with citation to Yu et al., 2021.

claim: Mesectoderm cells subsequently form the midline of the central nervous system, giving rise to specific neuronal and glial progeny.
source: They subsequently form the midline of the central nervous system, giving rise to specific neuronal and glial progeny (Wheeler et al., 2008) under the control of the Notch regulated single-minded gene, which is essential for cell division after gastrulation, acquisition of their midline fate and proper axonal connectivity (Nambu et al., 1990; Nambu et al., 1991; Hummel et al., 1999).
evidence: This is stated directly in the manuscript text with citations to Wheeler et al., 2008.

claim: The single-minded gene is Notch regulated and essential for cell division after gastrulation, acquisition of midline fate and proper axonal connectivity.
source: They subsequently form the midline of the central nervous system, giving rise to specific neuronal and glial progeny (Wheeler et al., 2008) under the control of the Notch regulated single-minded gene, which is essential for cell division after gastrulation, acquisition of their midline fate and proper axonal connectivity (Nambu et al., 1990; Nambu et al., 1991; Hummel et al., 1999).
evidence: This is stated directly in the manuscript text with citations to Nambu et al., 1990; Nambu et al., 1991; Hummel et al., 1999.

claim: Defects in the establishment of the mesectoderm boundary result in mixing of the left and right neuroectoderm as well as later effects on midline development.
source: Defects in the establishment of the mesectoderm boundary result in mixing of the left and right neuroectoderm as well as later effects on midline development (Yu et al., 2021).
evidence: This is stated directly in the manuscript text with citation to Yu et al., 2021.

claim: Two Notch-responsive enhancers, sim and m5/m8, undergo a transition approximately 50 min into nc14, when transcription levels increase approximately twofold.
source: A notable feature of the transcriptional profiles from two Notch-responsive enhancers, sim and m5/m8, is that they undergo a transition approximately 50 min into nc14, when transcription levels increase approximately twofold (Falo-Sanjuan et al., 2019).
evidence: This is stated directly in the manuscript text with citation to Falo-Sanjuan et al., 2019.

claim: The transition in transcription levels occurs as the embryo undergoes gastrulation.
source: This transition occurs as the embryo undergoes gastrulation, making it plausible that mechanical forces or tissue reorganization at this stage are responsible for the increase in transcription, and may contribute to the integrity of boundary formation (Nambu et al., 1990; Yu et al., 2021).
evidence: This is stated directly in the manuscript text describing the temporal correlation between the transcription transition and gastrulation.

claim: Gastrulation initiates toward the end of nc14, approximately 3 hr post fertilization.
source: Gastrulation initiates toward the end of nc14, approximately 3 hr post fertilization.
evidence: This is stated directly in the manuscript text describing the timing of gastrulation.

claim: During gastrulation, the apical surface of the most ventral subset of mesoderm (ME) cells constricts and cells shorten along their apico-basal axis.
source: During this process, the apical surface of the most ventral subset of mesoderm (ME) cells constricts and cells shorten along their apico-basal axis (Leptin and Grunewald, 1990; Sweeton et al., 1991).
evidence: This is stated directly in the manuscript text with citations to Leptin and Grunewald, 1990; Sweeton et al., 1991.

claim: Apical constriction during gastrulation occurs in response to apical re-localization of Myosin II (MyoII), which is controlled by a GPCR cascade.
source: This occurs in response to apical re-localization of Myosin II (MyoII), which is controlled by a GPCR (G-protein coupled receptor) cascade (Sweeton et al., 1991; Manning et al., 2013; Parks and Wieschaus, 1991; Barrett et al., 1997; Kölsch et al., 2007; Dawes-Hoang et al., 2005).
evidence: This is stated directly in the manuscript text with citations to multiple sources.

claim: The ventral furrow is formed as a consequence of apical constriction, which invaginates bringing the remainder of the mesoderm cells with it.
source: As a consequence, the 'ventral furrow' is formed, which invaginates bringing the remainder of the mesoderm cells with it (Leptin and Grunewald, 1990; Sweeton et al., 1991).
evidence: This is stated directly in the manuscript text with citations to Leptin and Grunewald, 1990; Sweeton et al., 1991.

claim: The force to invaginate the furrow is produced autonomously in the mesoderm by pulses of acto-myosin contractions.
source: Studies of the forces generated indicate that, although the force to invaginate the furrow is produced autonomously in the mesoderm by pulses of acto-myosin contractions (Martin et al., 2009), the mechanical properties of tissues adjacent to it, such as the MSE and neuroectoderm (NE), also change and may be important to allow invagination to occur (Rauzi et al., 2015).
evidence: This is stated directly in the manuscript text with citation to Martin et al., 2009.

claim: The mechanical properties of tissues adjacent to the mesoderm, such as the MSE and neuroectoderm (NE), also change and may be important to allow invagination to occur.
source: Studies of the forces generated indicate that, although the force to invaginate the furrow is produced autonomously in the mesoderm by pulses of acto-myosin contractions (Martin et al., 2009), the mechanical properties of tissues adjacent to it, such as the MSE and neuroectoderm (NE), also change and may be important to allow invagination to occur (Rauzi et al., 2015).
evidence: This is stated directly in the manuscript text with citation to Rauzi et al., 2015.

claim: There is a strong correlation between the start of mesoderm invagination and the time at which transcription levels increased.
source: Strikingly, we found a strong correlation between the start of mesoderm invagination and the time at which transcription levels increased.
evidence: This is stated directly in the manuscript text as a key finding.

claim: A Notch-independent vnd enhancer exhibited similar albeit more modest effect of gastrulation on transcription.
source: A Notch-independent enhancer exhibited similar albeit more modest effect, suggesting that the mechanism involves a more general feature.
evidence: This is stated directly in the manuscript text as a key finding.

claim: The Notch intracellular fragment, NICD, was also subject to similar regulation by gastrulation.
source: Furthermore, the Notch intracellular fragment, NICD, was also subject to similar regulation.
evidence: This is stated directly in the manuscript text as a key finding.

claim: The gastrulation-induced effect on transcription cannot be attributed to forces exerted on Notch receptor activation.
source: As a similar gastrulation-induced effect was detected when transcription was elicited by the intracellular domain NICD, it cannot be attributed to forces exerted on Notch receptor activation.
evidence: This is stated directly in the manuscript text as a key conclusion from the NICD experiments.

claim: Gastrulation-associated forces act on the nucleus to modulate transcription levels.
source: Together, these observations argue that gastrulation-associated forces act on the nucleus to modulate transcription levels.
evidence: This is stated directly in the manuscript text as a key conclusion.

claim: The regulation of transcription by gastrulation was uncoupled when the complex linking the nucleoskeleton and cytoskeleton (LINC) was disrupted.
source: This regulation was uncoupled when the complex linking the nucleoskeleton and cytoskeleton (LINC) was disrupted, indicating a likely conduit.
evidence: This is stated directly in the manuscript text as a key finding.

claim: The LINC complex is a likely conduit for the effects of gastrulation on transcription.
source: This regulation was uncoupled when the complex linking the nucleoskeleton and cytoskeleton (LINC) was disrupted, indicating a likely conduit.
evidence: This is stated directly in the manuscript text as a conclusion from the LINC disruption experiments.

claim: The coupling between tissue-level mechanics from gastrulation and enhancer activity represents a general mechanism for ensuring correct tissue specification during development.
source: We propose that the coupling between tissue-level mechanics, arising from gastrulation, and enhancer activity represents a general mechanism for ensuring correct tissue specification during development and that Notch-dependent enhancers are highly sensitive to this regulation.
evidence: This is stated directly in the manuscript text as a proposed general mechanism.

claim: Notch-dependent enhancers are highly sensitive to regulation by gastrulation-associated mechanics.
source: We propose that the coupling between tissue-level mechanics, arising from gastrulation, and enhancer activity represents a general mechanism for ensuring correct tissue specification during development and that Notch-dependent enhancers are highly sensitive to this regulation.
evidence: This is stated directly in the manuscript text as a proposed conclusion.

claim: Prior to ligand binding, the ADAM10 cleavage site in Notch is hidden by the negative regulatory region (NRR).
source: Prior to ligand binding, the ADAM10 cleavage site in Notch is hidden by the negative regulatory region (NRR).
evidence: This is stated directly in the manuscript text describing the Notch activation mechanism.

claim: Ligand binding exerts a force on the Notch receptor, leading to a displacement of the NRR to reveal the ADAM10 cleavage site.
source: To reveal this site, ligand binding exerts a force on the receptor, leading to a displacement of the NRR (Gordon et al., 2007; Gordon et al., 2015).
evidence: This is stated directly in the manuscript text with citations to Gordon et al., 2007; Gordon et al., 2015.

claim: A second cleavage by γ-secretase releases the intracellular domain, NICD, which forms a complex with a DNA-binding transcription factor and a co-activator to regulate transcription of target genes.
source: A second cleavage by γ-secretase then releases the intracellular domain, NICD, which forms a complex with a DNA-binding transcription factor and a co-activator to regulate transcription of target genes.
evidence: This is stated directly in the manuscript text describing the Notch signaling pathway.

claim: In many developmental processes, Notch activation occurs contemporaneously with morphological changes which could modulate pathway activity.
source: In many developmental processes, Notch activation occurs contemporaneously with morphological changes which could modulate pathway activity so that signaling and tissue rearrangements are coordinated (Paolini et al., 2021; Han et al., 2021; Engel-Pizcueta and Pujades, 2021; Lloyd-Lewis et al., 2019).
evidence: This is stated directly in the manuscript text with citations to multiple sources.

claim: Cell shape or tension changes in neighboring cells could impact on the forces exerted on the Notch receptor to alter the amount of cleavage.
source: For example, cell shape or tension changes in the neighboring cells could impact on the forces exerted on the receptor to alter the amount of cleavage (Shaya et al., 2017).
evidence: This is stated directly in the manuscript text with citation to Shaya et al., 2017.

claim: Mechanical forces could alter the transcriptional output from Notch activation by changing transport through nuclear pores or altering chromatin compaction.
source: Alternatively, mechanical forces could alter the transcriptional output from Notch activation, by changing transport through nuclear pores or altering chromatin compaction (Boumendil et al., 2019; Gozalo et al., 2020).
evidence: This is stated directly in the manuscript text with citations to Boumendil et al., 2019; Gozalo et al., 2020.

claim: 30-45% of MSE nuclei exhibit a clear, circa twofold, transition in m5/m8 transcription levels.
source: Thus, when m5/m8 transcription profiles from individual nuclei were analyzed, a clear, circa twofold, transition in levels was detected in 30–45% of the MSE nuclei (Figure 1C).
evidence: This is stated directly in the manuscript text with reference to Figure 1C.

claim: The observed increase in the mean transcriptional activity was not due to an increase in the number of active cells.
source: The observed increase in the mean transcriptional activity was not due to an increase in the number of active cells (Figure 1D), but rather to a change in the profiles within individual nuclei.
evidence: This is stated directly in the manuscript text with reference to Figure 1D.

claim: α-Cat KD led to the most severe disruption of gastrulation where mesoderm cells failed to invaginate and divided externally.
source: Of the three tested, α-Cat KD led to the most severe disruption of gastrulation; mesoderm cells failed to invaginate and divided externally (Figure 2—figure supplement 1A-C, Video 2).
evidence: This is stated directly in the manuscript text with reference to Figure 2—figure supplement 1A-C and Video 2.

claim: No increase in m5/m8 [II]-directed transcription occurred in α-Cat KD embryos.
source: Strikingly, no increase in m5/m8 [II]-directed transcription occurred in these embryos. Instead, the mean levels decreased after the initial activation, at the time when the increase in levels normally occurs, and then plateaued at a lower level (Figure 2B, Figure 2—figure supplement 2B).
evidence: This is stated directly in the manuscript text with reference to Figure 2B and Figure 2—figure supplement 2B.

claim: Depletion of either Cta or RhoGEF2 resulted in a slowing of gastrulation.
source: Depletion of either Cta or RhoGEF2 resulted in a slowing of gastrulation. Cta depletion also caused variable delays in the start of mesoderm invagination (Figure 2—figure supplement 2BC; Video 3).
evidence: This is stated directly in the manuscript text with reference to Figure 2—figure supplement 2BC and Video 3.

claim: In Cta or RhoGEF2 depleted embryos, there was no normal increase in transcription at the time of gastrulation.
source: In neither genotype was there a normal increase in transcription at the time of gastrulation. The mean levels remained similar to those prior to gastrulation and, on an individual nucleus basis, very few exhibited any marked change in levels (Figure 2D, Figure 2—figure supplement 2CD).
evidence: This is stated directly in the manuscript text with reference to Figure 2D and Figure 2—figure supplement 2CD.

claim: fog- hemizygous embryos exhibited a delayed start of mesoderm invagination and slowed gastrulation overall.
source: fog- hemizygous embryos exhibited a delayed start of mesoderm invagination and slowed gastrulation overall (Figure 2—figure supplement 1BC Video 2).
evidence: This is stated directly in the manuscript text with reference to Figure 2—figure supplement 1BC and Video 2.

claim: The vnd early embryonic enhancer (vndEEE) is active throughout nc14 and drives expression in a band of cells that overlap the MSE.
source: Unlike many of the other embryonic enhancers studied to date, the vnd early embryonic enhancer (vndEEE) is reported to be active throughout nc14 and to drive expression in a band of cells that overlap the MSE (Stathopoulos et al., 2002).
evidence: This is stated directly in the manuscript text with citation to Stathopoulos et al., 2002.

claim: A new MS2 reporter containing the vnd enhancer was active from the beginning of nc14 throughout gastrulation and recapitulated the spatial pattern of vnd.
source: As predicted, a new MS2 reporter containing this enhancer, referred to here as vnd, was active from the beginning of nc14 throughout gastrulation and recapitulated the spatial pattern of vnd (Video 4).
evidence: This is stated directly in the manuscript text with reference to Video 4.

claim: The proportion of nuclei that exhibited a clear increase in vnd transcription levels was considerably lower than for m5/m8 (16% of MSE nuclei and 2% of NE nuclei).
source: The proportion of nuclei that exhibited a clear increase in levels when considered individually was, however, considerably lower than for m5/m8 (16% of MSE nuclei and 2% of NE nuclei, Figure 3C).
evidence: This is stated directly in the manuscript text with reference to Figure 3C.

claim: vnd is not regulated by Notch.
source: As there is no evidence that vnd is regulated by Notch (Markstein et al., 2004), this implies that gastrulation exerts effects on transcription independent of any effects on Notch activation.
evidence: This is stated directly in the manuscript text with citation to Markstein et al., 2004.

claim: Notch RNAi treatment greatly reduced transcription from m5/m8 [II].
source: To verify that the modulation of vnd is not Notch dependent, we used an RNAi line to deplete Notch levels. As predicted, this treatment greatly reduced transcription from m5/m8 [II] (Figure 3—figure supplement 1A,B).
evidence: This is stated directly in the manuscript text with reference to Figure 3—figure supplement 1A,B.

claim: The mean profile of m5/m8 [II] transcription in MSE nuclei exposed to ectopic NICD had two peaks, the first shortly after the onset of NICD expression and the second during gastrulation.
source: The mean profile of m5/m8 [II] transcription in MSE nuclei that were exposed to NICD had two peaks, the first shortly after the onset of NICD expression and the second during gastrulation.
evidence: This is stated directly in the manuscript text describing the transcription profile with ectopic NICD.

claim: The second peak of m5/m8 transcription with ectopic NICD was initiated at the start of mesoderm invagination, characteristic of the gastrulation-induced increase in transcription in normal conditions.
source: Thus, the second 'peak' was initiated at the start of mesoderm invagination, characteristic of the gastrulation-induced increase in transcription in normal conditions.
evidence: This is stated directly in the manuscript text describing the timing of the second peak.

claim: No transcription was detected outside the domain of the eve2 stripe in Notch RNAi depleted embryos with ectopic NICD, confirming that Notch depletion was successful.
source: No transcription was detected outside the domain of the eve2 stripe (Figure 4—figure supplement 1A, Video 5), confirming that Notch depletion was successful.
evidence: This is stated directly in the manuscript text with reference to Figure 4—figure supplement 1A and Video 5.

claim: MSE nuclei within the stripe where NICD was expressed exhibited the same profile of activity in Notch RNAi depleted embryos as those from control embryos with intact Notch.
source: Strikingly, MSE nuclei within the stripe where NICD was expressed exhibited the same profile of activity in Notch RNAi depleted embryos to those from control embryos with intact Notch. In particular, the levels of transcription increased at the time of gastrulation and to the same degree (Figure 4AC).
evidence: This is stated directly in the manuscript text with reference to Figure 4AC.

claim: The transition in transcription levels at gastrulation occurs even in the absence of full-length Notch, arguing the effects are downstream of receptor cleavage.
source: Thus, the transition in transcription levels at gastrulation occurs even in the absence of full-length Notch, arguing the effects are downstream of receptor cleavage.
evidence: This is stated directly in the manuscript text as a conclusion from the NICD experiments in Notch-depleted embryos.

claim: In α-Cat depleted embryos with ectopic NICD, where gastrulation was completely disrupted, there was no second peak of transcription from m5/m8 [II].
source: In the α-Cat depleted embryos, where gastrulation was completely disrupted, there was no second 'peak' of transcription from m5/m8 [II]. Instead the levels remained at low levels from the time when mesoderm invagination would normally occur (Figure 4AC).
evidence: This is stated directly in the manuscript text with reference to Figure 4AC.

claim: Gastrulation exerts differential impacts across the ectoderm, which might be related to the gradients of forces and cell deformation that have been measured.
source: Furthermore, the consequences are strongest in MSE cells, suggesting that gastrulation exerts differential impacts across the ectoderm, which might be related to the gradients of forces and cell deformation that have been measured (Fuse et al., 2013; Rauzi et al., 2015).

claim: No difference was found in the area of mesectoderm cells that exhibited increased m5/m8 [II] transcription compared to their neighbors where there was no marked increase.
source: We found no difference in the area of mesectodem cells that exhibited increased m5/m8 [II] transcription compared to their neighbors where there was no marked increase (Figure 5—figure supplement 2B) nor in the eccentricity or length of their contact with mesoderm cells.
evidence: This is stated directly in the manuscript text with reference to Figure 5—figure supplement 2B.

claim: As there was no distinct transition at the time of mesoderm invagination in klar knockdown embryos, this suggests there is an uncoupling of the transcription profiles from the gastrulation movements caused by LINC complex disruption.
source: As there was no distinct transition at the time of mesoderm invagination, this suggests there is an uncoupling of the transcription profiles from the gastrulation movements caused by LINC complex disruption.

claim: klar knockdown embryos exhibited longer and less robust gastrulation.
source: However, as these embryos exhibited longer and less robust gastrulation (Figure 5C, Figure 5—figure supplement 2C) it is not possible to fully rule out that the lack of a normal increase in transcription are the result of these indirect effects on gastrulation.

claim: None of the fluorescently-tagged molecules of different dimensions (including dextrans and GFP variants) exhibited any change in nuclear levels at the time of gastrulation.
source: We first investigated whether there were any general changes in the nuclear import properties by analyzing the nuclear levels, and nuclear exclusion, of fluorescently-tagged molecules of different dimensions, including fluorescently-tagged dextrans of two molecular weights (70 kDa and 40 kDa), as well as several tagged variants of GFP, with and without a nuclear localization signal (nls). None of these exhibited any change in nuclear levels at the time of gastrulation, (Figure 6—figure supplement 1AB), including 70kDa-FITC dextran which exhibited the highest nuclear exclusion (Figure 6—figure supplement 1A), consistent with previous data (Hampoelz et al., 2016).
evidence: This is stated directly in the manuscript text with reference to Figure 6—figure supplement 1AB.

claim: Twist levels increase in the mesoderm throughout nc14, but no clear change or additional increase in nuclear levels occurred in mesectoderm cells at the time of gastrulation.

evidence: This is stated directly in the manuscript text with reference to Figure 6AB and Video 7.

claim: During gastrulation, mesoderm nuclei decrease the longest axis and increase the second (i.e. they become shorter and wider) and mesectoderm nuclei do so to a greater extent than those in the neuroectoderm but less than those in the mesoderm.
